doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

chapter: Joe Williams as singer and recording artist
title: Joe's gospel album Feel the Spirit
summary: Joe long wanted to record a giving-thanks gospel album; Telarc's John Snyder made it happen, with Marlena Shaw, proceeds to a scholarship fund.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I’ve noticed Joe seems to be spreading his wings. This new CD that’s about to be released or has just been released. Tell us about that one.

Has been — “Feel the Spirit”? That’s something Joe has, did he tell you about that? It’s something he’s wanted to do for absolutely ever since I’ve known him. Because years ago his great friend was Jimmy Jones, who was a wonderful piano player and arranger. And I’ve heard him discuss that with Jimmy back in the early 60’s that he had this in mind to, he calls it a giving thanks, a giving back for all the fun and pleasure he’s had I suppose, and he’s been dying to do it. He never could get it on, no one was interested in recording it, until John Snyder of Telarc said he would like to do it and so finally it’s been achieved and he’s happy with it I think.
I’ve heard most of it, yes.

I love some of it, yes. You know that Gospel stuff, you can hardly keep still, and he’s got Marlena Shaw on some of them too, and she is a knockout. So it’s really fun and he loves it. And he’s giving the proceeds to a scholarship fund I think.
I don’t know about that one, or whether he’s going to work up another one. But that’s his way of giving back he says.
